rulings.challenge_claim: The row attaches a 3-verse digit to a quoted spelling that stands in exactly one verse, silently blending two unnamed attested spellings, and states the motto's framing relation backwards against the bytes.
rulings.grounds: Digit sub-claim REFUTED: the row's "one of three amar-qohelet third-person intrusions... (sweep: 3 verses)" cites the pre-established tier-1 DEVICE FAMILY (eccl_device_inventory.json frame_seams.amar_qohelet_formula: count=3, refs Eccl.1.2/7.27/12.8, count_object explicitly "verses whose skeleton matches the said-qohelet formula (אמר/אמרה + optional article, either spelling)"), matching TOOLKIT.md/book_strategy section 2a verbatim ("amar-qohelet third-person frame intrusions at 1:2, 7:27, 12:8") -- owner-ratified, not a writer invention. OL's own sweep of the literal contiguous string "אָמַ֣ר קֹהֶ֔לֶת" (=1 verse) tests a DIFFERENT object (a bare skeleton substring) than the family the row actually named; that sub-claim does not hold. Directional sub-claim UPHELD: collate.py byte tier on oshb:Eccl.1.2 confirms the verse runs "הֲבֵ֤ל הֲבָלִים֙..." then "אָמַ֣ר קֹהֶ֔לֶת" then "הֲבֵ֥ל הֲבָלִ֖ים הַכֹּ֥ל הָֽבֶל" -- the said-formula sits VERSE-MEDIAL, bracketed BY the two superlative doublings, not the reverse. The row's "carries the superlative doubling twice... framed by the said-qohelet formula" inverts this order. Non-fatal: the row's actual frame_narration-over-wisdom_poem warrant rests on the said-formula marking third-person reported speech (register argument), not on this spatial framing detail, so the row's unit_type call is not undermined.
rulings.remedy: Replace "carries the superlative doubling twice in one verse, framed by the said-qohelet formula..." with a verse-medial statement (e.g. "the said-qohelet formula... sits verse-medial, bracketed by the two superlative doublings"). Test: collate.py byte-tier re-check on oshb:Eccl.1.2 confirming the corrected clause matches token order; no change needed to the 3-verse family digit or its refs.

rulings.challenge_claim: The four-image series is enumerated out of byte order, and the row's 'internal bracket' framing of the under-the-sun refrain conceals its third chapter-1 member past the row's own closing seam; the 'no first-person marker' universal is contested.
rulings.grounds: All three sub-claims byte-confirmed. (a) Order: bytes run generations דּ֤וֹר הֹלֵךְ֙ וְד֣וֹר בָּ֔א (Eccl.1.4), sun וְזָרַ֥ח הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ (Eccl.1.5), wind הוֹלֵ֣ךְ הָר֔וּחַ (Eccl.1.6), rivers כָּל הַנְּחָלִים֙ (Eccl.1.7) -- i.e. generations FIRST, sun, wind, rivers; the row's boundary_rationale lists "sun, wind, rivers, generations," out of order. (b) eccl_device_inventory.json under_the_sun.tachat_hashemesh gives chapter-1 count=3 (refs Eccl.1.3, 1.9, 1.14) -- the device_note's "refrain bracket internal to this row" names only 1:3/1:9 and omits 1:14, which sits in the immediately following row of this cluster (P01-004, Eccl.1.12-1.15), i.e. the refrain resumes unbroken one verse past this row's own 1:11|1:12 seam, undisclosed -- a CROSS-SEAM COHESION gap. (c) The universal "no first-person marker... anywhere inside it" is contradicted at the byte level: Eccl.1.10 carries מִלְּפָנֵֽנוּ (a 1cp pronominal suffix, "before us"). The narrower, defensible claim -- no standalone אני token in Eccl.1.3-1.11 -- IS true (sweep.py --skel אני = 25 verses book-wide, first at Eccl.1.12, matching eccl_device_inventory.json first_person_ani), but that is not what the row stated.
rulings.remedy: (1) Reorder the image list to generations/sun/wind/rivers per bytes. (2) Revise the device_note to disclose the Eccl.1.14 tachat-hashemesh recurrence immediately past the row's own seam per cross-seam-cohesion, rather than calling 1:3/1:9 a closed internal bracket. (3) Narrow "no first-person marker" to "no standalone אני token" (matching the first_person_ani inventory). Test: sweep.py --skel re-check on the corrected order and narrowed claim; eccl_device_inventory.json under_the_sun re-check for the disclosure.

rulings.challenge_claim: strongest_rejected_alternative names 'the toolkit's frame-spine sweep' as authority -- a production-tooling reference in row prose, forbidden by the register-purge rule.
rulings.grounds: Byte-confirmed against the row's own text: strongest_rejected_alternative reads "...which the toolkit's frame-spine sweep tracks as a distinct first-person speech verb." This names the review/production apparatus itself ("the toolkit," "frame-spine" is a literal TOOLKIT.md section header) as the evidentiary authority rather than arguing from the verse's own bytes. The standing REGISTER PURGE rule bars file-order/process talk in row prose without exception; the sole sanctioned shorthand is the "(sweep: N verses)" convention, used correctly elsewhere in this very cluster (P01-001 "(sweep: 4 verses)", P01-002 "(sweep: 3 verses)"). This is a hygiene defect independent of whether the underlying dibbarti/natati distinction is itself sound (see the separate OL item on this row for that question).
rulings.remedy: Strike the apparatus reference and replace with a byte-grounded clause naming the device directly, e.g. "a distinct first-person speech verb (דברתי, sweep: 2 verses) from the natan root of 1:13" -- no tool/process noun. Test: the campaign's own register-purge check must return zero tool/process-noun hits on the revised row prose.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's sole boundary warrant (dibbarti vs natati) is falsified one verse inside its own span, and dibbarti's only other site opens nothing.
rulings.grounds: Byte-confirmed: Eccl.1.13 reads וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת לִבִּ֗י לִדְר֤וֹשׁ וְלָתוּר֙... (natan+lev+lamed-infinitive-of-cognition). Eccl.1.16, the row's claimed restart, reads דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי אֲנִ֤י עִם לִבִּי֙.... But Eccl.1.17 -- ONE VERSE INSIDE this row's own span -- reads וָאֶתְּנָ֤ה לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת..., the SAME natan+lev+lamed-infinitive-of-cognition construction as 1:13 (both WEB renderings track this: 'applied my heart to seek/search' // 'applied my heart to know'). The construction the row treats as belonging to the PRECEDING unit recurs undisclosed inside the very row it is used to separate from that unit -- a CROSS-SEAM COHESION violation. Compounding this: sweep.py --skel דברתי = exactly 2 verses (Eccl.1.16, Eccl.2.15); at 2:15 the form is verse-medial (וְאָמַ֨רְתִּֽי אֲנִ֜י בְּלִבִּ֗י... ודברתי בלבי) and opens no row in this cluster's own chunking (2:15 sits mid-span inside P01-008, Eccl.2.11-2.16). A 2-site form whose only other occurrence is boundary-irrelevant cannot alone certify 1:16 as a restart. לבי itself threads unbroken through 1:13/1:16/1:17/2:1/2:3/2:15 (sweep.py --skel לבי = 14 verses), i.e. a shared heart-formula runs straight through every seam this row and its neighbors cut.
rulings.remedy: Revise the boundary_rationale/strongest_rejected_alternative to disclose the 1:17 natan-construction recurrence and drop the implied clean natan-vs-dibbarti binary; if 1:15|1:16 is retained as a boundary, ground it in the dibbarti LEXEME itself (genuinely a new verb, even though the surrounding heart-idiom persists), not in an implied wholesale formula shift. Test: collate.py byte-tier on oshb:Eccl.1.17 vs oshb:Eccl.1.13 confirming the shared construction; sweep.py --skel דברתי confirming the 2-site digit and 2:15's non-boundary status in the current row set.

rulings.challenge_claim: The amarti opener does not discriminate a boundary: it recurs twice inside this two-verse row, recurs verse-initially in a neighbouring row where it opens nothing, and shares its be-libbi idiom with the verse it is said to be distinct from.
rulings.grounds: (a) sweep.py --skel אמרתי = 9 verses including BOTH Eccl.2.1 (אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י) and Eccl.2.2 (...אָמַ֣רְתִּי) -- the token recurs twice inside this row's own two verses, so it cannot by itself certify the row's OPENING. (b) The fuller 3-token formula אמרתי אני בלבי recurs verse-initially at Eccl.2.15 (וְאָמַ֨רְתִּֽי אֲנִ֜י בְּלִבִּ֗י...) yet opens no row in this cluster's own chunking -- 2:15 sits mid-span inside the neighbouring row P01-008 (Eccl.2.11-2.16), an inconsistency in how the writer applies the same restart-marker logic across this row set. (c) בלבי is shared between 2:1 and Eccl.2.3 (תַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י...; sweep.py --skel בלבי = 5 verses), so the rejected_alternative's claim that 2:3 opens under "a new heart-formula" overstates the change -- only the verb (תַּ֣רְתִּי vs אמרתי) differs, not the prepositional idiom. (d) The device_note's "(1:2's occurrences belong to the frame motto, outside this row)" implies no prior monologue-internal hevel, but Eccl.1.14 (וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַכֹּ֛ל הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ, inside the preceding row P01-004, itself inside the monologue) already carries the bare token -- 2:1 is not as early an occurrence as the phrasing implies.
rulings.remedy: Ground the 2:1 opening in something more discriminating than the bare amarti recurrence, or disclose/resolve the 2:15 inconsistency together with P01-008's remedy; correct "new heart-formula" to name the verb (תַּ֣רְתִּי) as what changes, not the idiom; revise the device_note to acknowledge the 1:14 monologue-internal precedent. Test: sweep.py --skel re-checks on אמרתי, אמרתי אני בלבי, and בלבי against the corrected claims.

rulings.challenge_claim: The rejected_alternative's syntactic warrant is byte-false -- MT 2:4 opens asyndetically with a finite verb, so a clause break stands exactly where the row asserts none.
rulings.grounds: Byte-confirmed: Eccl.2.3 closes its own clause at מִסְפַּ֖ר יְמֵ֥י חַיֵּיהֶֽם, and Eccl.2.4 opens הִגְדַּ֖לְתִּי מַעֲשָׂ֑י -- a finite 1cs perfect verb with NO leading conjunction (asyndetic; verse_map_oshb.json direct inspection). Asyndeton is a clause break; the row's stated warrant ("no clause break between them") does not hold. A genuine, byte-true binder is available and un-claimed instead: the ethical-dative לי runs Eccl.2.4-2.9 (6 consecutive verses, confirmed against consonantal_index.json) and מכל שהיה/שהיו לפני בירושלם recurs at 2:7 and 2:9 -- real lexical cohesion that should replace the false syntactic claim. Secondary: the device_note's characterization of 3:1-8 as "the fixed et-plus-infinitive register template" overstates its own opening verse -- Eccl.3.1 pairs וְעֵ֥ת with וְעֵ֥ת לְכָל חֵ֖פֶץ (no infinitive); the et+lamed-infinitive pattern begins at Eccl.3.2 (עֵ֥ת לָלֶ֖דֶת...). Tertiary: the parenthetical "(natan/tur versus tarti)" mislabels the comparison -- Eccl.2.3's תַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י shares its root (תור) with 1:13's וְלָתוּר֙, not with וְנָתַ֣תִּי (a separate root, נתן); the parenthetical does not name what actually differs (verb form: finite vs. infinitive) versus what is shared (root תור).
rulings.remedy: Replace the 'no clause break' syntactic warrant with the confirmed lexical-cohesion argument (ethical dative לי, Eccl.2.4-2.9; the mikol...lifnay-bi-Yerushalaim inclusio at 2:7/2:9); soften the 3:1-8 characterization to locate the et+infinitive template at 3:2-8 with 3:1 as the introductory heading; correct the root-comparison parenthetical to name the shared root (תור) vs. the differing verb form. Test: verse_map_oshb.json direct check of 2:3/2:4 confirming the asyndetic break; consonantal_index.json check of לי scoped to 2:4-2:9; consonantal_index.json check of 3:1 vs 3:2 for the infinitive-template onset.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's opening verse (2:11) carries a verdict clause skeleton-identical to 1:14 and unique to those two verses, undisclosed -- the row never addresses the stronger rival that 2:11 is the retrospective close of the 1:12-2:11 experiment sequence rather than an opener paired with 2:12.
rulings.grounds: sweep.py --skel והנה הכל הבל ורעות רוח (with vehinneh) returns exactly 2 verses book-wide: Eccl.1.14 and Eccl.2.11, nowhere else. Eccl.1.14 sits inside the immediately PRECEDING row of this cluster (P01-004, Eccl.1.12-1.15) and is never named in this row's boundary_rationale, device_notes, or strongest_rejected_alternative. Eccl.2.11 also reuses יתרון (וְאֵ֥ין יִתְר֖וֹן תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ) -- sweep.py --skel יתרון = 9 verses including Eccl.1.3 (the book's opening question) and Eccl.2.11, inside the same tachat-hashemesh formula. 2:11's own opening clause וּפָנִ֣יתִֽי אֲנִ֗י בְּכָל מַעֲשַׂי֙... backward-references the anaphoric building/planting/accumulation catalogue of Eccl.2.4-2.8 (the row immediately before this one, P01-007) via shared vocabulary (מעשי, echoing 2:4's הִגְדַּ֖לְתִּי מַעֲשָׂ֑י), rather than anticipating 2:12's wisdom-versus-folly inquiry. None of this backward-pulling evidence is disclosed; the row's strongest_rejected_alternative addresses only the internal 2:11/2:12 split, never the unaddressed rival that 2:11 is the retrospective verdict-close of the entire 1:12-2:11 sequence (echoing 1:14's identical formula) rather than an opener paired forward with 2:12. This is a CROSS-SEAM COHESION violation bearing directly on the row's own core forward-pairing warrant, not a mere prose-precision issue. The row's own stated forward-pairing evidence (פניתי, Eccl.2.11+2.12 only, sweep-confirmed) is itself genuine and unique -- the defect is the undisclosed backward-pulling rival at the row's own opening seam.
rulings.remedy: Minimum cure: disclose the 1:14/2:11 skeleton-identical verdict-clause echo and the backward-referencing maasi/amalti vocabulary link to 2:4-2:8 in the boundary_rationale or strongest_rejected_alternative, explaining why 2:11 is kept with 2:12 despite it. PROPOSAL ONLY (requires boss/owner adoption): the writer wave may reconsider whether 2:11 more properly closes P01-007 (extending its span to 2:3-2:11) with a new row opening cleanly at 2:12. Test: sweep.py --skel והנה הכל הבל ורעות רוח must return exactly {Eccl.1.14, Eccl.2.11}, and the revised rationale must name and address this rival explicitly.

rulings.challenge_claim: The verdict device this row cites as its own evidence recurs one verse past its closing seam at consonantally identical strength (2:17), undisclosed, while a much smaller internal repetition is disclosed.
rulings.grounds: sweep.py --skel הכל הבל ורעות רוח (without vehinneh) returns exactly 3 verses book-wide: Eccl.1.14, Eccl.2.11, Eccl.2.17. Eccl.2.17 -- the FIRST verse immediately past this row's own 2:16|2:17 closing boundary -- carries כִּֽי הַכֹּ֥ל הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ, accent_stripped-identical to the recurrence inside the row at 2:11. The tachat-hashemesh formula compounds this: present at 2:11 (inside the row), absent 2:12-2:16, then resumes unbroken at 2:17-2:20 immediately outside (eccl_device_inventory.json under_the_sun.tachat_hashemesh ch.2 refs include 2:11, 2:17, 2:18, 2:19, 2:20). Per CROSS-SEAM COHESION, a byte-true device straddling the row's own closing seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed; the row discloses only its smaller INTERNAL 2:11/2:12 פניתי repetition (itself confirmed accurate) and says nothing about the denser recurrence at its lower boundary. Separately: Eccl.2.15 opens וְאָמַ֨רְתִּֽי אֲנִ֜י בְּלִבִּ֗י... -- the identical formula a neighbouring row of this cluster (P01-006) treats as its own unit-opening driver at 2:1 -- yet 2:15 sits mid-span inside THIS row without comment; the two rows' boundary logic is not disclosed as mutually consistent.
rulings.remedy: Revise device_notes to disclose the 2:17 recurrence of the verdict clause and the tachat-hashemesh resumption immediately past the row's closing seam; either argue explicitly why 2:16|2:17 remains the correct boundary despite this pull, or flag the tension for the writer wave. Resolve consistently with the P01-006 remedy regarding the 2:15/2:1 amarti-ani-be-libbi formula. Test: sweep.py --skel הכל הבל ורעות רוח must return {Eccl.1.14, Eccl.2.11, Eccl.2.17}; eccl_device_inventory.json under_the_sun re-check for 2:17-2:20 resumption.
